name: Visualization
definition: The ability to imagine how something will look after it is moved around or when its parts are moved or rearranged.

benchmark.name: ShapeNet-SRN
benchmark.human_reference: General adult workforce performing everyday spatial visualization (imagining how a familiar object such as a chair or car looks from another viewpoint), benchmarked against typical mental-rotation competence.

benchmark.name: SPARE3D
benchmark.metric: accuracy (%) per task; no single aggregate metric

benchmark.name: CLEVR-MRT
benchmark.model_or_system: The authors' self-supervised 3D contrastive volumetric encoder with a camera-conditioned FILM VQA head (Beckham et al.)
benchmark.human_reference: General adult workforce performing everyday spatial visualization, such as imagining a simple scene of a few objects from another viewpoint.

benchmark.name: SPARE3D
benchmark.model_or_system: Self-supervised spatial reasoning network (Xiang et al., CVPR 2022)
benchmark.metric: accuracy (%) on the SPARE3D 3-View to Isometric (T2I) 4-way multiple-choice task
benchmark.human_reference: General adult / relevant educated workforce (untrained adults performing everyday or technical spatial visualization, e.g., reading multi-view drawings)

benchmark.name: SPACE
benchmark.metric: average accuracy (%) across the 10 small-scale SPACE tasks, multimodal presentation; chance is below 25%
benchmark.human_reference: General adult workforce. Classic psychometric visualization tests (MRT, form board, perspective taking) are normed on general adults and students.

benchmark.name: SpatialViz-Bench
benchmark.metric: accuracy (%) on multiple-choice questions, averaged over all 1,180 items
benchmark.human_reference: Relevant educated workforce: adults who routinely do spatial visualization work, such as technicians, drafters and engineering-adjacent workers. The published human baseline (82.46%) most likely comes from educated adult participants.

benchmark.name: SpatialViz-Bench
benchmark.human_reference: General adult / educated workforce performing everyday spatial visualization at work, such as technicians, trades workers, drafters and assemblers. Psychometric-style mental rotation, paper folding and cube-net tasks are standard aptitude items for this population.
